newsitem.title: CHINA: SWIMMING-CHINA'S MEN'S OLYMPIC TEAM TO STAND TALL.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CHINA'S MEN'S OLYMPIC TEAM TO STAND TALL.

text.p: China's men's swimming team, who finished outside the medals at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, will be looking for taller swimmers in future, state media and officials said on Wednesday.
The Liberation Army Daily quoted assistant national team coach Zhou Ming as saying China would try to select men's swimmers at least 1.90 metres tall.
Sports officials said China was aiming to strengthen its swimming team in time for the 2000 Olympics in Sydney.
"Height is really an advantage in swimming," a national team official told Reuters.
But he said the height requirement would prove difficult to meet as relatively few athletes in China measured up.
Jiang Chengji, who stands 1.91 metres tall, put in the best performance of China's men's swimming team at the Atlanta Games, finishing fourth in both the 100 metres butterfly and 50 metres freestyle.
China's men's team have never matched the successes of the nation's women swimmers, who have landed a rich haul of world and Olympic titles in the 1990s.
